Півчетвертої ночі закінчили термінові правки на нашому сервері. Причина в тому, що в світі знайшли дві критичні вразливості в самій мові PHP. Їх назвали PHP2Shell, це CVE-2026-109618 і CVE-2026-109619. Оцінка 9.2 з 10, а для експлуатації не потрібна авторизація.

Основна наша система написана іншою мовою, але кілька окремих сервісів працювали на PHP. Ми несемо відповідальність за все, що крутиться на нашому сервері, тому закрили всі.

Що відомо станом на зараз.

Виправлення вийшли 21 жовтня у версіях 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 та 8.2.35. Старші гілки офіційних патчів не отримали.

Знайшли діри дослідники з допомогою моделей ШІ: першу версію компанія Calif ще в серпні, а Wiz незалежно виявила обидві. Дослідники кажуть, що вада існувала роками, але ШІ зробив її експлуатацію практичною.

Інформація витекла за день до виходу патчу. Спроби атак фіксували ще 17 жовтня, за кілька днів до публічного розкриття. Деякі уряди, за повідомленнями, на час відключили свої сайти.

Масштаб. PHP стоїть на близько 70% сайтів, де відома серверна мова. Це не означає, що стільки зламано: надійних цифр підтверджених зломів поки немає, і дослідники пишуть, що експлуатація складніша, ніж здавалось у перший день. Але ризик реальний, а старих версій без підтримки в мережі дуже багато.

Що зробити вам.

Перевірте, чи є PHP на сервері та в контейнерах: php -v, docker images.
Оновіть PHP і перезапустіть php-fpm або веб-сервер.
Якщо оновитись не можете одразу, вимкніть session.upload_progress.enabled.
Подивіться на дивні дочірні процеси від користувача веб-сервера і нові php файли.
Якщо сервіси були відкриті в мережі з 17 жовтня, змініть ключі та токени.

Бережіть себе і свої сервери 🙏

posts.content:
----------------

🛠️ Tool
===================

php2shell-scanner: high-fidelity exposure detection for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619

Searchlight Cyber's research team (the group formerly known as Assetnote) released an open-source scanner for the php2shell vulnerability pair. The team has been through this cycle before, both with wp2shell, which it discovered itself, and with react2shell late last year. Each of these high-impact web-stack issues raises the same detection problem: maximize coverage while minimizing false positives and false negatives. This release is their answer for the current one.

Why another scanner

Scanners published in the wake of the disclosure mostly rely on version checks, or fail to represent the vulnerable conditions accurately for both mod_php and php-fpm. Version-only signals fail in two directions: flagging hosts that are actually patched, or missing hosts where the banner does not reflect exploitable conditions. The logic was first implemented inside the Searchlight Exposure platform, and the standalone version is now public.

How the check works

Detection is progressive, in three tiers:

1. Controlled OOM trigger. The scanner attempts to produce a PHP memory-exhaustion error. The vulnerability fundamentally requires an out-of-memory condition, so there is no reliable way to confirm exploitability without inducing it.
2. Differential empty HTTP 500. Next, it observes responses for a differential empty HTTP 500, which the authors describe as a PHP-FPM worker failure.
3. Version fallback. Only when behavioral checks do not settle the question does it fall back to whether the target advertises a known unpatched PHP version.

Risk profile

The authors are direct about this: triggering an OOM condition is inherently risky, and that is the price of reliable detection here. In the majority of PHP installations a worker crash recovers quickly and should not cause disruption, but the writeup explicitly asks for care and caution when scanning. Practical translation: don't fire this at capacity-constrained production systems during peak traffic.

Context around the disclosure

Initial information on the vulnerability was incomplete, followed quickly by a wave of auto-generated, low-quality PoCs that added noise rather than clarity. Searchlight credits Calif's writeup with settling most of the open questions. The detection logic served Searchlight Exposure customers first, then was released publicly so anyone can determine exposure with the same rigor.

Practical notes
• Exposure validation across mixed PHP estates where mod_php and php-fpm behave differently
• Prioritization: behavioral tiers are stronger evidence than version matches
• Scheduling: run behavioral checks away from peak load, and treat the version fallback tier as weaker evidence by design
• The tool is newly released and not personally tested; this summary reflects the vendor writeup, not an independent accuracy assessment

References
• Repository: assetnote/php2shell-scanner on GitHub
• Authors: Shubham Shah, Adam Kues, Patrik Grobshäuser, Kevin Gervot
• Related: Calif's writeup on php2shell

posts.content:
Півчетвертої ночі закінчили термінові правки на нашому сервері. Причина в тому, що в світі знайшли дві критичні вразливості в самій мові PHP. Їх назвали PHP2Shell, це CVE-2026-109618 і CVE-2026-109619. Оцінка 9.2 з 10, а для експлуатації не потрібна авторизація.

Основна наша система написана іншою мовою, але кілька окремих сервісів працювали на PHP. Ми несемо відповідальність за все, що крутиться на нашому сервері, тому закрили всі.

Що відомо станом на зараз.

Виправлення вийшли 21 жовтня у версіях 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 та 8.2.35. Старші гілки офіційних патчів не отримали.

Знайшли діри дослідники з допомогою моделей ШІ: першу версію компанія Calif ще в серпні, а Wiz незалежно виявила обидві. Дослідники кажуть, що вада існувала роками, але ШІ зробив її експлуатацію практичною.

Інформація витекла за день до виходу патчу. Спроби атак фіксували ще 17 жовтня, за кілька днів до публічного розкриття. Деякі уряди, за повідомленнями, на час відключили свої сайти.

Масштаб. PHP стоїть на близько 70% сайтів, де відома серверна мова. Це не означає, що стільки зламано: надійних цифр підтверджених зломів поки немає, і дослідники пишуть, що експлуатація складніша, ніж здавалось у перший день. Але ризик реальний, а старих версій без підтримки в мережі дуже багато.

Що зробити вам.

Перевірте, чи є PHP на сервері та в контейнерах: php -v, docker images.
Оновіть PHP і перезапустіть php-fpm або веб-сервер.
Якщо оновитись не можете одразу, вимкніть session.upload_progress.enabled.
Подивіться на дивні дочірні процеси від користувача веб-сервера і нові php файли.
Якщо сервіси були відкриті в мережі з 17 жовтня, змініть ключі та токени.

Бережіть себе і свої сервери 🙏

posts.content:
----------------

🛠️ Tool
===================

php2shell-scanner: high-fidelity exposure detection for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619

Searchlight Cyber's research team (the group formerly known as Assetnote) released an open-source scanner for the php2shell vulnerability pair. The team has been through this cycle before, both with wp2shell, which it discovered itself, and with react2shell late last year. Each of these high-impact web-stack issues raises the same detection problem: maximize coverage while minimizing false positives and false negatives. This release is their answer for the current one.

Why another scanner

Scanners published in the wake of the disclosure mostly rely on version checks, or fail to represent the vulnerable conditions accurately for both mod_php and php-fpm. Version-only signals fail in two directions: flagging hosts that are actually patched, or missing hosts where the banner does not reflect exploitable conditions. The logic was first implemented inside the Searchlight Exposure platform, and the standalone version is now public.

How the check works

Detection is progressive, in three tiers:

1. Controlled OOM trigger. The scanner attempts to produce a PHP memory-exhaustion error. The vulnerability fundamentally requires an out-of-memory condition, so there is no reliable way to confirm exploitability without inducing it.
2. Differential empty HTTP 500. Next, it observes responses for a differential empty HTTP 500, which the authors describe as a PHP-FPM worker failure.
3. Version fallback. Only when behavioral checks do not settle the question does it fall back to whether the target advertises a known unpatched PHP version.

Risk profile

The authors are direct about this: triggering an OOM condition is inherently risky, and that is the price of reliable detection here. In the majority of PHP installations a worker crash recovers quickly and should not cause disruption, but the writeup explicitly asks for care and caution when scanning. Practical translation: don't fire this at capacity-constrained production systems during peak traffic.

Context around the disclosure

Initial information on the vulnerability was incomplete, followed quickly by a wave of auto-generated, low-quality PoCs that added noise rather than clarity. Searchlight credits Calif's writeup with settling most of the open questions. The detection logic served Searchlight Exposure customers first, then was released publicly so anyone can determine exposure with the same rigor.

Practical notes
• Exposure validation across mixed PHP estates where mod_php and php-fpm behave differently
• Prioritization: behavioral tiers are stronger evidence than version matches
• Scheduling: run behavioral checks away from peak load, and treat the version fallback tier as weaker evidence by design
• The tool is newly released and not personally tested; this summary reflects the vendor writeup, not an independent accuracy assessment

References
• Repository: assetnote/php2shell-scanner on GitHub
• Authors: Shubham Shah, Adam Kues, Patrik Grobshäuser, Kevin Gervot
• Related: Calif's writeup on php2shell

For some reason, the CVE-2026-111497 buffer overflow vulnerability in the #brotli decoder is mostly associated with #nodejs, but this is a far wider issue. Brotli compression is supported by many client-side applications processing HTTP responses. While some of them have sandboxes and a quick update cycle (read: web browsers), many don't. In particular, many devices and applications using #curl / libcurl are affected and must be updated ASAP.

CVE-2026-115931.description:
Postiz lets a signed-in user ask the backend to run a function on one of their connected channels. The backend did not restrict which functions can be requested, so a user could call internal helper functions that were never meant to be reachable from the web interface.

One of those helpers reads a file from the server's disk. A user who connects a channel whose stored token is a file path can have the backend return the contents of any file it can read, including its environment, which holds the secret used to sign login sessions, the database address and the credentials of connected services. Another helper makes the backend process exit with a single request. Self-registration is open by default, so no existing account and no action by another user is needed.

CVE-2026-115806.description: The Prime Mover – Backup and Migration plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.2.1 via deserialization of untrusted input in the migration search-and-replace routine (recursiveUnserializeReplace()). An unauthenticated attacker can store a crafted, base64-encoded serialized object in wp_comments.comment_content through the standard comment-submission endpoint (wp-comments-post.php). When an administrator subsequently performs a routine Prime Mover export or restore, the plugin base64-decodes that stored value and passes it to unserialize() with no allowed_classes restriction. A Property-Oriented Programming (POP) chain is present in the plugin's own bundled Freemius library (FS_Clone_Manager::__set → FS_Option_Manager::set_option → store() → update_option()), so no additional plugin or theme is required — the plugin ships the gadget itself.

CVE-2026-91403.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: JSSE).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511, 8u511-perf, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5, 27.0.1; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21 and  21.0.13; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. posts.content: CVE-2026-87858 Temporal: header-based trust check lets an authenticated caller send internal callbacks, enabling RCE. CVSS 9.9. Patch under review - apply mitigations now. #CVE #infosec #cybersecurity https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-87858/

CVE-2026-87858.description: Temporal Server decided whether a Workflow completion callback was internal by reading a caller-supplied HTTP header. An authenticated caller holding only write permission in a single namespace could attach a completion callback whose URL host matched the configured callback address allowlist, whose URL path was any Temporal HTTP API route, and whose header map contained a non-empty header named source. When the History service delivered that callback, the non-empty source header caused it to re-target the request at the local frontend client and rewrite only the scheme and host, preserving the caller's path, query, and request body. Where an internal frontend is deployed with its HTTP API enabled, that client resolves to the internal frontend, which authorizes every request as a system administrator without requiring authentication information. The result is that the server performs an attacker-chosen state-changing HTTP POST against its own administrative API on the caller's behalf, in namespaces where the caller has no permission. The caller never needs network access to the internal frontend, because the History service makes the request. Confirmed effects include terminating Workflows in other namespaces, registering namespaces, modifying another namespace's configuration, and deleting another namespace and its Workflows. The affected routing logic is present in both the HSM and CHASM callback delivery implementations. This description and the CVSS score in this record describe releases 1.30.0 and later, where any non-empty source header is sufficient. Releases 1.25.0 through 1.29.7 are affected by a narrower form of the same defect in which the header must exactly match a configured cluster ID, a UUID that a namespace-scoped caller cannot read through the API. The consequence once that match occurs is the same, but the attack is materially harder and scores lower. To determine whether a deployment is affected, check two settings together: the static Server configuration for a non-zero services.internal-frontend.rpc.httpPort, and the effective per-namespace dynamic configuration value of component.callbacks.allowedAddresses. A deployment is exposed only when an internal frontend is deployed with a non-zero HTTP port, at least one allowlist rule admits a host, and authorization is enabled. The allowlist is empty by default, which denies all external callback URLs, and the stock static topology does not include an internal frontend. Note that a failed attach returns the error 'invalid url: url does not match any configured callback address', which proves only that one tested URL did not match and does not prove the effective allowlist is empty. To look for callbacks already attached, use DescribeWorkflowExecution, which returns callback information for a Workflow's registered completion callbacks. Operators should be aware of a gap when searching for evidence of delivery: the frontend HTTP API server records the request method and URL at debug level only, so at default log levels a delivered request is not written to the internal frontend's logs, and the absence of such log entries is not evidence that the issue was not exploited.

CVE-2026-94368.description: A flaw was found in the signature verification logic of noobaa-core, the core component of the NooBaa Multicloud Object Gateway. The issue occurs when the service processes S3 presigned URLs using Signature Version 4 (SigV4). Due to improper validation, the service fails to reject requests containing unsigned x-amz- headers, instead simply dropping them from the signature calculation. This allows an attacker who possesses a valid presigned PUT URL to add an unsigned x-amz-copy-source header, effectively converting a simple upload into a CopyObject operation. This can lead to unauthorized access and copying of any data the original signer is permitted to reach across the entire storage system.

ReqLLM.Streaming.WebSocketSession.Client.start/3 in lib/req_llm/streaming/web_socket_session/client.ex starts WebSockex without TLS options, and WebSockex defaults to insecure: true, which connects with verify: :verify_none. The OpenAI Responses, Realtime, and Codex WebSocket paths reach this client and send the API key or OAuth access token in the authorization header. HTTP streaming through Finch and the HTTP/2 duplex session through Mint verify certificates and are not affected.

This issue affects req_llm: from 1.9.0 before 1.29.0.

Wasmtime is a runtime for WebAssembly. Prior to 36.0.19 and 43.0.0, the Cranelift compiler backend bit-packs SSA value indices in a way that can silently overflow in release builds when compiling a sufficiently large or specially crafted Wasm func...

CVE-2026-115889.description:
## Summary

In Wasmtime prior to v43, the Cranelift compiler backend bit-packs its SSA value indices in a way that can result in silent overflow in release builds, and result in incorrect value references in the IR resulting in arbitrary miscompilation. A very large Wasm function body, or one that is specially crafted to use many SSA values, can use this to force type-confusion or other arbitrary side-effects and escape the sandbox.

Cranelift was changed in Wasmtime v43 to use a full `u32` index, with checks if that limit is exceeded, and so is no longer susceptible to this bug.

## Impact

A Wasmtime engine with default settings (using the Cranelift backend) on any architecture/platform could experience a sandbox escape from a specially-crafted Wasm module.

## Patches

Wasmtime v36.0.19 has been released which fixes this issue.

The newly disclosed vulnerability is separate from the two PHP2Shell flaws patched earlier this week and is not fixed by PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35.
⠀
PHP says exploitation requires an unusual configuration where an application:

• Uses php_binary or php_serialize as its session serializer
• Changes the serializer to php at runtime before session_start()
• Has session upload progress enabled
⠀
PHP considers the risk unlikely and plans to release a fix during its next regular update cycle.

Until then, administrators with affected configurations should set:

session.upload_progress.enabled=0

Applications that do not change the session serializer at runtime are not exposed through this path.

No exploitation has been reported.

Source:

CVE-2026-115938.description:
Craft CMS allows any authenticated control panel user to submit an element-search condition whose element selector is evaluated as a sandboxed Twig object template. Craft’s allowed column filter delegates property lookup to Yii ArrayHelper, outside Twig’s SecurityPolicy. Repeated single-segment lookups therefore bypass the sandbox’s empty property/method allowlists.



The vulnerable condition value is ultimately cast to an integer. That does not protect the secret: the template can return author ID 1 when a guessed key character is correct and an impossible ID otherwise. The JSON endpoint returns entries for the first case and an empty array for the second, forming a stable remote character oracle.



After recovering GeneralConfig::securityKey, the same user can compute Craft’s generic HMAC wire format offline. Signed parameters such as redirect are then accepted and passed to unsandboxed View::renderObjectTemplate(), where Twig’s string-callable form can invoke native PHP callables. The regression proof uses the harmless substr() callback and observes abcdef becoming cdef; it does not execute an OS command.

The app/process-api-response-headers action accepts fake Craft API response headers from any authenticated control panel user.



A non-admin user with only accessCp can place newline characters in X-Craft-Plugin-Licenses. Craft passes this value to its .env writer without removing the newlines.

CVE-2026-79982.description:
The Bluetooth HCI USB transport class of the new USB device stack, subsys/usb/device_next/class/bt_hci.c, copies every controller-to-host HCI packet into a USB transfer buffer before enqueuing it on an endpoint. bt_hci_tx_sync_in() allocated that buffer from bt_hci_ep_pool, a fixed pool whose slots are only USBD_MAX_BULK_MPS bytes (64 on full-speed-only builds), and then performed net_buf_add_mem(buf, bt_buf->data, bt_buf->len) with no length check. HCI event and ACL buffers are sized by CONFIG_BT_BUF_EVT_RX_SIZE and CONFIG_BT_BUF_ACL_RX_SIZE and can be far larger, so the copy runs past the end of the 64-byte slot into the adjacent slots and into whatever follows the statically allocated pool.

The device runs the local Bluetooth controller in raw HCI mode (CONFIG_BT_HCI_RAW), so the oversized packets originate over the air. With the HCI buffer sizes recommended for full-featured controllers, an unauthenticated attacker within Bluetooth range can supply the overflowing bytes: a connected peer that negotiates Data Length Extension can send ACL fragments up to CONFIG_BT_CTLR_DATA_LENGTH_MAX bytes, and an attacker that merely broadcasts extended advertising data reaches the same path through LE Extended Advertising Report events, which the controller fragments only to CONFIG_BT_BUF_EVT_RX_SIZE. In the stock configuration the overflow is already reached without any radio traffic: the mandatory Read Supported Commands command-complete event is 70 bytes and overruns the 64-byte slot by six bytes on every host initialization.

Because net_buf_add_mem() validates tailroom only through an assertion unless CONFIG_NET_BUF_HARDENING is enabled, builds with CONFIG_ASSERT=n — the usual production setting — silently corrupt memory adjacent to the USB buffer pool with attacker-chosen contents, which on a target without memory protection between subsystems can lead to arbitrary code execution. Builds with assertions enabled fail the assertion instead and panic, giving a remotely triggerable denial of service. The fix introduces a separate bt_hci_tx_pool sized to MAX(BT_BUF_ACL_RX_SIZE, BT_BUF_EVT_RX_SIZE) for the controller-to-host direction while leaving the host-to-device pool at the endpoint packet size, which is already bounds-checked during reassembly.

Ruby has released versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 to address three memory corruption bugs in its Onigmo regular expression engine.
⠀
The flaws involve a double free and two integer overflow conditions. GitLab found that specially crafted regex patterns could trigger the bugs and potentially allow remote code execution.

Four GitLab vulnerabilities rely on the underlying issues:

• CVE-2026-89078
• CVE-2026-93577
• CVE-2026-97229
• CVE-2026-110264
⠀
Applications are only exposed when they compile regular expressions from attacker-controlled input. Ruby warns that Regexp.timeout and pattern length limits do not reliably prevent exploitation.

Administrators should update to Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 or 3.3.13 and avoid compiling untrusted regex patterns if an immediate upgrade is not possible.

• CVE-2026-97229

CVE-2026-115419 - Unintended disclosure of data element to wrong session in Strands Agents SDK A2A Server

Bulletin ID: 2026-146-AWS Scope: AWS Content Type: Important (requires attention) Publication Date: 10/22/2026 13:00 PM PDT

Strands Agents is an open-source SDK, available for Python and TypeScript, for building AI ...

#aws #security

CVE-2026-115419.description:
**Summary**  
Strands Agents SDK is an open-source SDK, available for Python (strands-agents) and TypeScript (@strands-agents/sdk), for building and running AI agents. An issue exists where, under certain circumstances, the Agent2Agent (A2A) server shares conversation history across callers with different context\_id values, allowing one caller to read and influence another caller's session.  
  
**Impact**  
The A2A server did not properly isolate conversation state between callers. In multi-tenant deployments, an authenticated remote user could access another caller's conversation history or influence model behavior for other callers (CWE-488: Unintended Disclosure of Data Element to Wrong Session). This affects any deployment where an A2A server is reachable by more than one user or tenant.  
  
**Impacted versions:**  
strands-agents (Python): all versions containing the multiagent.a2a module, < 1.43.0  
@strands-agents/sdk (TypeScript): < 1.5.0  
  
**Patches**  
This issue has been addressed in strands-agents version 1.43.0 and @strands-agents/sdk version 1.5.0. The A2A server now uses an agent factory so conversation state is isolated per A2A context\_id. We recommend upgrading to the latest version and ensuring any forked or derivative code is patched to incorporate the new fixes.  
  
**Workarounds**  
There is no workaround that fully addresses this issue in affected versions. Until you upgrade, do not expose an A2A server to more than one user or tenant. If multiple callers need access, run a separate A2A server instance for each user or tenant.  
  
**References**  
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, we ask that you contact AWS Security via our [vulnerability reporting page](https://aws.amazon.com/security/vulnerability-reporting) or directly via email to [aws-security@amazon.com](mailto:aws-security@amazon.com). Please do not create a public GitHub issue.

"Signal has resolved a critical-severity vulnerability that could allow a malicious caller to keep audio and video tracks enabled even after the user hung up.

The security defect is tracked as CVE-2026-113380 (CVSS score of 9.3) and impacts RingRTC, the open source library Signal uses for voice and video calls, which is based on WebRTC.

Due to the issue, a remote peer could flood the call’s Finite State Machine (FSM) event queue with junk, and the call would not terminate.

This happened because the hangup was not treated as a kill switch, but as an event added to the FSM event queue; there was no rate limit on peer-originated events; and the hangup event had no priority.

“Flood the queue with junk and the hang-up waits behind attacker noise forever, so the call (microphone, possibly camera) is never torn down,” a GitHub write-up by a researcher reads.

By exploiting the vulnerability, an attacker could keep the audio and video tracks flowing from a target device while the victim believes they ended the call.

The security defect was resolved in RingRTC version 2.72.0, which was released on September 4.

Details on the flaw, however, were published on Tuesday, along with a conceptual proof-of-concept (PoC). NIST added the CVE to the NVD database on Tuesday.

Signal resolved the issue by ensuring that call termination requests do not remain blocked in FSM’s event queue and are detected independently.

Users should update their Signal applications as soon as possible. Otherwise, they should check the call indicator to make sure the call indeed ended."

Patch to 2.12.1+ and restrict user permissions. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-54630-cwe-434-unrestricted-upload-of-file-with-dangerous-type-in-part-db-part-db-server-3e3f77096f8d900f #OffSeq #CVE #RCE #infosec

CVE-2026-54630.description: Part-DB is an open source inventory management system for electronic components. Prior to version 2.12.1, the part attachment upload handler stores uploaded files under the web-served media directory using the client-supplied file extension, and its extension blocklist does not include phar. AttachmentSubmitHandler::renameBlacklistedExtensions() rewrites dangerous extensions (php, phtml, sh, cgi, py, js, html, htaccess, ...) to .txt, but phar is absent from the list, so a .phar file keeps its extension. Public attachments (the default) are written into public/media/, which is the Apache document root. The shipped Apache configuration routes .phar to PHP-FPM, so the stored file is executed as PHP on request. The per-attachment-type extension filter is empty by default and is not consulted by the upload handler in a way that blocks this, and a non-admin user in the default users group can create an attachment type with no filter and attach files to parts. Any authenticated user in the default users group uploads a .phar attachment to a part and fetches it under /media/, executing arbitrary PHP as the www-data web user. Ability to exploit depends on the webserver config, docker image contained the vulnerability by default. This issue has been patched in version 2.12.1.
